subtitle: Commercial policies with stacked endorsements, coverage sublimits, and conditional exclusions require a tool that can hold the whole document in context. That is what Claude does.

consistency_blocks.bottom_line: Claude is the strongest AI for insurance work that involves long, complex policy documents. Reviewing a full commercial package policy, comparing coverage between expiring and renewal, or identifying coverage gaps across multiple policies are tasks where Claude's 1M-token context window creates a meaningful difference. For quick client emails and coverage explanations, ChatGPT is faster. For serious document analysis, Claude is the right tool.
consistency_blocks.key_takeaway: › 1M-token context window handles full commercial policies including base form plus all endorsements; › Can compare coverage provisions across expiring and renewal policies to flag meaningful differences; › Strong for drafting coverage analysis narratives, proposal sections, and long client-facing reports
consistency_blocks.best_for: Reviewing full commercial policies with multiple endorsements and schedules; Comparing expiring vs. renewal policy to identify coverage changes and gaps; Drafting long-form coverage analysis reports for commercial clients; Identifying exclusions and conditions that affect coverage for a specific risk; Producing coverage summaries from complex multi-policy programs
consistency_blocks.avoid_if: You need current carrier rates, underwriting appetite, or live pricing data; You need current state regulatory guidance or recent compliance updates; You are handling simple personal lines work where ChatGPT is faster and sufficient; You want AI embedded directly in Word, Excel, or Outlook (use Copilot instead); Your agency hasn't reviewed AI usage policy for policy document analysis
consistency_blocks.mini_workflow: Copy the relevant sections of the expiring policy and the renewal policy (base forms and key endorsements) → Paste both into Claude with the prompt below asking for a comparison → Review Claude's comparison against the original documents to verify accuracy → Use the verified comparison as preparation notes for the renewal conversation

content_sections.section_body:
The core use case for Claude in commercial insurance is reviewing policies that are too long or complex for simpler tools to handle effectively. Standard personal lines policies, a homeowners or auto policy, are well within ChatGPT's capability. A complex commercial program with stacked endorsements and multiple lines is where Claude's context advantage becomes material.

Identifying key exclusions and coverage conditions

Commercial policies are full of exclusions, conditions, and definitions that interact with each other. An exclusion in one endorsement may be modified by another. A coverage condition may eliminate a coverage that appears to exist in the base form. Claude can review the full policy, base form plus all endorsements, and identify the provisions that most affect the client's actual coverage for their specific type of operation.

Always verify Claude's exclusion analysis against the actual policy language. Exclusions are the provisions most likely to matter when a claim occurs, and mischaracterizing an exclusion to a client creates real E&O exposure.

Expiring-to-renewal comparison

At renewal, clients and brokers both want to know what changed from the expiring policy. Carriers make coverage changes at renewal that are disclosed in endorsements that are easy to overlook. Claude can review both policies simultaneously and produce a structured list of meaningful differences: coverage limits that changed, exclusions that were added or removed, conditions that changed, endorsements that were added or deleted.

Prompt to try in Claude

I am pasting the relevant sections of two commercial general liability policies: the expiring policy (clearly labeled) and the renewal policy (clearly labeled). Please compare them and produce: (1) a list of any coverage changes, limits, sublimits, or coverage grants that changed; (2) a list of any exclusions that were added to the renewal that were not in the expiring policy; (3) any exclusions that were removed; (4) any endorsement changes. Flag any change that could materially affect coverage for a general contractor with residential and commercial work. I will verify all findings against the original policy language.

Verify all comparison findings against both source policy documents. Do not rely on AI analysis alone for coverage advice. Include no client PII.

Commercial clients, especially larger accounts, often receive coverage analysis reports that explain their program, identify gaps, and document coverage recommendations. These reports are time-consuming to produce from scratch. Claude can draft the analysis narrative from structured notes or from the policy documents themselves, producing a first draft that the professional reviews, corrects, and personalizes.

Drafting coverage analysis narratives

From a structured outline of the client's coverage program, Claude can produce a narrative that explains the coverage structure, notes key limitations, identifies coverage gaps relative to the client's risk profile, and explains the recommendations. The quality of the output depends on the quality of the input: specific, accurate notes from the professional's analysis produce better output than vague general descriptions.

Coverage gap identification for specific industries

For clients in specific industries, contractors, technology companies, healthcare-adjacent businesses, certain coverage gaps are predictable. Claude can review a client's current program and identify standard coverage gaps for their industry, which the professional then verifies, adds to, and uses as the basis for coverage recommendations. This is faster than starting the gap analysis from a blank framework each time.

Prompt to try in Claude

I am pasting the declarations pages and key endorsements from a commercial policy for a technology consulting firm. Please review the coverage and identify: (1) any common technology professional liability exposures that appear to be uninsured or underinsured, (2) any cyber liability gaps relative to standard coverage for a firm of this type, (3) whether the general liability form covers technology professional services or excludes them. Flag anything you cannot determine from the policy text with [NEEDS DIRECT REVIEW]. I will verify all findings against the full policy.

Verify all gap analysis findings against the full policy forms. Technology coverage requirements vary significantly by operation type.

content_sections.section_title: Long-Form Proposals and Coverage Recommendation Letters
content_sections.section_body:
Commercial insurance proposals often include substantial written narrative: background on the client's risk profile, an explanation of the recommended coverage structure and why it was selected, a description of key coverage features, and a summary of the program's strengths and limitations. Claude's writing quality and extended context make it well-suited for drafting these longer documents.

Executive summaries for complex programs

For a commercial client reviewing a complex insurance program, an executive summary that explains the overall structure, the key coverages, and any areas where coverage was difficult to obtain or has meaningful limitations is more useful than the full proposal document. Claude can draft this summary from an outline of the program, producing a client-ready document the professional reviews and personalizes.

Prompt to try in Claude

Based on the program outline below, draft a 400-500 word executive summary for a commercial client. The summary should cover: (1) the overall structure of their insurance program (lines of coverage included), (2) the key coverage features and limits, (3) one area where coverage was constrained by market conditions and what that means for their risk, and (4) one specific recommendation for coverage enhancement at their next renewal. Write in a clear, professional tone accessible to a business owner who is not an insurance expert.

Fill in your actual program details. Review all coverage descriptions against the actual policies before sending to the client.

content_sections.section_title: Where Claude Falls Short for Insurance Professionals
content_sections.section_body:
No current carrier or market data
Claude does not know current carrier appetite, underwriting guidelines, rate environments, or market conditions. For current carrier and pricing research, use your agency management system, carrier portals, and industry resources. Claude handles document analysis; it does not replace market knowledge.
No current regulatory or state-specific guidance
Insurance regulations change frequently at the state level. Claude's training has a cutoff and may not reflect current state insurance department requirements, recent filing changes, or new coverage mandates. For current regulatory guidance, usePerplexity AIto find and verify primary source documents.
Can mischaracterize specific coverage language
Claude can produce plausible-sounding but inaccurate interpretations of specific policy provisions, particularly for unusual endorsements, jurisdiction-specific forms, or provisions that interact with each other in non-obvious ways. All coverage analysis must be verified against the original policy language by the licensed professional before client use.
Not embedded in office productivity tools
Claude is a standalone chat interface. If you need AI assistance directly inside Word, Excel, or Outlook for your proposal and correspondence workflow,Microsoft Copilotoffers better integration. Many professionals use both: Claude for document analysis,Copilotfor the M365 writing workflow.

Comparing your options? Also see ChatGPT, Copilot for insurance professional, and Perplexity AI for insurance professional. For the full picture, visit our Claude overview or the complete AI tools for insurance professionals guide.

faq.question: Can Claude review a full commercial insurance policy?
faq.answer: Yes. Claude's 1M-token context window can handle very long commercial policies including base forms, endorsements, and schedules in a single session. It can identify coverage gaps, summarize exclusions, compare provisions between renewal and expiring, and answer specific questions about the policy without losing context across sections.

faq.question: How does Claude compare to ChatGPT for insurance policy review?
faq.answer: Claude is significantly better for long or complex policies. ChatGPT has a smaller context window and may miss provisions in longer commercial policies when reviewing the full document. Claude's 1M-token window allows the entire policy, base form plus endorsements, to be reviewed in a single session with full context. For shorter personal lines policies, both tools handle the task adequately.

faq.question: Can Claude identify coverage gaps between two policies?
faq.answer: Yes. Claude can compare coverage provisions across two policies simultaneously, for example, comparing a client's current policy to a proposed replacement at renewal, and identify meaningful differences in coverage, exclusions, limits, and conditions. Always verify Claude's comparison against the original policy documents before relying on it for client advice.

faq.question: Is Claude useful for drafting coverage proposals and client reports?
faq.answer: Yes. Claude can draft long-form coverage analysis reports, proposal narratives, and client-facing coverage summaries from structured notes or outlines. Its writing quality for extended, nuanced documents is strong. All drafts require review for accuracy against actual policy terms before client distribution.

faq.question: Does Claude have current insurance carrier or pricing data?
faq.answer: No. Claude does not have access to current carrier rates, underwriting guidelines, or state-specific regulatory changes since its training cutoff. For current regulatory research, use Perplexity AI. Claude handles document analysis and writing; Perplexity handles current information lookup.

faq.question: How should insurance professionals manage E&O risk when using Claude?
faq.answer: All AI-generated coverage descriptions, policy summaries, and recommendations must be verified against the actual policy language before distribution to clients. Claude can miss nuanced provisions or mischaracterize specific coverage terms. The licensed professional bears the responsibility for accuracy. Never distribute AI-generated coverage analysis to clients without independent review.

insights.insight_title: The context window is the differentiator for commercial work
insights.insight_body: Reviews that test ChatGPT and Claude against simple, short policy documents miss where Claude pulls ahead. A personal auto policy is 30 pages. A commercial package for a mid-size contractor might be 150 pages after you stack all endorsements. Claude holds the full 150 pages in context. ChatGPT doesn't. For commercial brokers, this is not an edge case, it is the core use case for every major account review.

insights.insight_title: The renewal comparison is the highest-value workflow
insights.insight_body: The specific workflow most underexplored by commercial brokers is using Claude to compare expiring and renewal policies. Carriers change coverage in endorsements that are buried in a large policy package and easy to miss. Claude can identify all the differences in minutes. A broker who catches a meaningful coverage reduction before the client signs the renewal has just demonstrated value that is very difficult to replicate with any other tool.

insights.insight_title: Claude and ChatGPT are a natural pair, not competitors
insights.insight_body: The right approach is Claude for the analysis, ChatGPT for the communication. Use Claude to review the policy, identify the gaps, and produce the coverage analysis. Use ChatGPT to draft the client email explaining what you found. Both tools cost about $20/month, and each excels at a different part of the commercial insurance workflow. Choosing one and trying to use it for everything produces worse results than using both appropriately.

reviews_miss.insight_banner: "Use Claude to read the policy. Use ChatGPT to explain what you found. Use Perplexity to find what changed in the market last month."
